claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has been reported in a hierarchical heterostructured state featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.

A multi-fidelity machine-learning model combining high-resolution microstructural images with physics-informed features will predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness of HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than current first-principles and computationally intensive methods.
The proposed model will predict these properties more efficiently than current first-principles and computationally intensive methods.
High-resolution images can capture the hierarchical heterostructure and multilevel chemical fluctuations relevant to mechanical-property prediction.
The multiscale chemical fluctuations and microstructural heterogeneity mediate the predictive relationship between structure and mechanical properties.
Convolutional neural networks can extract fine-grained spatial features from the microstructural images.
Combining image-derived spatial features with CALPHAD and simplified-simulation features enables the model to learn nonlinear mappings to mechanical performance.
Avoiding extensive first-principles simulations reduces the computational cost of property prediction.
The reduced-computation strategy can maintain or improve prediction accuracy.
The model is expected to reduce prediction errors for Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness by approximately 25–30% relative to traditional approaches.
The model is expected to improve computational efficiency by up to one order of magnitude relative to traditional approaches.
Prior full first-principles calculations and high-dimensional machine-learning methods required high computational resources and had low efficiency.
Parameter sweeps and direct simulations of fracture processes were computationally prohibitive.
The approach may become unreliable when image resolution is insufficient to capture the relevant heterogeneities.
The approach may become unreliable when processing or testing significantly alters the hierarchical microstructural state.
The approach may become unreliable when the dataset is too limited or unrepresentative to capture property–structure variability.
Toughness prediction has greater uncertainty than prediction of Young’s modulus or yield strength because of the complexity of fracture dynamics.
